slides.texte_overlay:
Social habits that make
people remember you for years
Sending a message on the hard days. A friend's exam, a funeral, a breakup. "Thinking of you today" takes ten seconds, and people remember it for the rest of their lives.
Celebrating small wins. Someone passed their driving test or got a new flat? Make a fuss. Being the person who gets excited for others is rare and unforgettable.
Asking for their opinion. "You know about this, what would you do?" People never forget the person who made them feel smart and valued in front of others.
Bringing new ideas into old friendships. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I always have something surprising to share when we meet.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I always have something surprising to share with my friends.

slides.texte_overlay: Remembering the first time you met. "I still remember you showing up soaked at that party." Shared memories told with warmth make people feel truly important.
Being generous with your time. Helping someone move, listening for an hour, driving them to the airport. Time is the gift people remember long after any present.
Ending every meeting with a plan to meet again. "Same time next month?" A simple invitation turns a good evening into a friendship that keeps going for years.
